entry.description: The child takes the word apart into parts she has met in other words and sums them. She has not mistaken which word it is — she has taken it apart, and the parts are real while the sum is not the word. Scoped to the ERROR, not to vocabulary items.
entry.childHint: The parts of a word do not always add up. Check the whole word in the sentence.

stem.text: Read lines 65 to 67. Mr Darcy says Elizabeth 'is tolerable: but not handsome enough to tempt me'. What does 'tolerable' mean here?

carriers.key: Only just good enough to look at.

options.value: Kind, and easy to get along with.
Good at putting up with things without complaining.
options.execution: The target is TOLERABLE. 'Putting up with things without complaining' is the meaning of TOLERANT, a different word the target resembles in form; the line is about how she looks. NOTE REPAIRED 2026-08-16 (delivery 52): this was described as 'a real second sense of the word' and it is not a sense of the target at all. Tag grandfathered under the era exception; a note that is wrong about English is not.

options.value: Only just good enough to look at.
Very good-looking, so he is paying her a compliment.
Too proud to dance with anybody.
